findings.title: Empty updateMany cannot bump SelectedCalendar.updatedAt
findings.body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) to refresh SelectedCalendar.updatedAt after writing cache. Prisma rejects updateMany when data is empty ("data must not be empty"), and even if it did not, @updatedAt is only rewritten when some other field changes. This runs after the cache upsert, so a successful Google cache refresh still throws and the timestamp the new status UI depends on is never updated.

findings.title: Deleting cache does not refresh connected-calendars data
findings.body: deleteCacheMutation only toasts and calls the optional onSuccess prop. Unlike the disconnect mutation in the same component, it never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars. SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper passes onChanged through and does not refetch that query itself, so after a successful delete the dropdown still shows the old cache timestamp and "Delete cached data" until a full reload.

findings.title: Cache status ignores expiry
findings.body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups every CalendarCache row for the credential and returns max(updatedAt) with no expiresAt >= now() filter. Expired rows still produce a cacheUpdatedAt, so CredentialActionsDropdown treats the credential as having live cache (hasCache is just a truthy timestamp) and offers delete for data the availability path will not serve.

findings.title: dev:cron now depends on undeclared tsx
findings.body: dev:cron was changed from ts-node (a declared devDependency of @calcom/web) to npx tsx, but tsx is not listed in this package. yarn dev:cron will download an arbitrary tsx via npx or fail offline/in CI, instead of using the previously pinned local runner.

findings.title: Env rewrite uses macOS-only sed
findings.body: The new webhook helper updates GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL with sed -i '' , which is BSD/macOS syntax. On GNU sed that form treats '' as the script and does not edit the file in place, so the script reports success while leaving .env unchanged on Linux.
